_comment: One entry per preset. `kt` is the figure the cited page prints, not a figure
chosen for roundness: where a page prints a range, `kt` takes a value inside
that range and `note` says which. `quote_yield` and `quote_year` are copied
verbatim from the cited page; scripts/check_weapons.py --online asserts both
strings are still on it, so a preset cannot outlive its source.
Nothing in this file describes an effect. The radii live in weapon-radii.json,
which scripts/build_weapon_radii.py derives from effects.json and Fig. 7.42.

presets.name: Little Boy
presets.note: Uranium gun-type bomb, the first used in war; dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945.

source.label: National Museum of Nuclear Science & History — Little Boy and Fat Man

presets.quote_yield: Explosive force: 15,000 tons of TNT equivalent

presets.name: Fat Man
presets.note: Plutonium implosion bomb, dropped on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

source.label: National Museum of Nuclear Science & History — Little Boy and Fat Man

presets.quote_yield: Explosive force: 21,000 tons of TNT equivalent

presets.name: W76-2
presets.yield_note: 5–7 kt published estimate; radii computed at the 6 kt midpoint
presets.note: Low-yield Trident II warhead. Every public figure is a 5–7 kt range rather than a point value, so the radii here are computed at the 6 kt midpoint of that range.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: W76-1
presets.note: Life-extended W76 for the Trident II missile, the most numerous warhead in the US stockpile.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: W87
presets.note: Warhead for the Minuteman III intercontinental missile.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: W88
presets.note: Trident II warhead; some older charts print a lower estimate, and this page uses the figure the linked page prints.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: B83
presets.note: Variable-yield strategic bomb; 1,200 kt is its highest setting, and a lower setting draws smaller rings.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: B53
presets.note: 9 Mt high-yield bomb, in service from 1962 until the last 50 were retired in 1997.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: Ivy Mike
presets.note: First true thermonuclear test, 1 November 1952; it was a surface burst, so the contact setting is the faithful one.

presets.name: Castle Bravo
presets.note: Largest US test, 1 March 1954; a surface burst that ran about 2.5 times its predicted yield.

presets.name: B41
presets.note: Highest-yield bomb the United States ever fielded, manufactured from 1960 and retired by 1976.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — Complete List of All U.S. Nuclear Weapons

presets.name: Tsar Bomba
presets.note: Largest weapon ever detonated, 1961; a 50 Mt air burst, and the blast figure the page prints is half its 100 Mt design.

source.label: Nuclear Weapon Archive — The Tsar Bomba
